To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the service sector is not a residual sector, that it is not a sector of low productivity and that it is not an unproductive sector, and, finally, that innovation in services is not a myth.

1) services and goods are not mutually exclusive categories; 2) innovation in services exists, but is not always easy to identify; 3) the service sector is innovative, although it is not always easy for it to innovate; and 4) the service economy is not a residual activity.

innovation in services is a reality; it takes a variety of forms; it is not necessarily more difficult than innovation in manufacturing; it does not necessarily require new organisational forms; it does require a different approach from that traditionally adopted by the manufacturing sector.
In summary, our research is concerned with
innovation in the service sector, and in particular with its relationship with the manufacturing sector.

the following questions: how is innovation in services organised? What are the main obstacles to innovation in this area? What forms can innovation in services take? What are the most important areas in which to promote innovation in services?

the following issues: the nature and extent of innovation in services and the myths that have surrounded it; the role of innovation in the development of service activities; the nature of the innovation process in services; the relationship between goods and services and their impact on the innovation process; the role of information and communication technologies (ICT) in the development of innovation in services; and the relationship between innovation in services and innovation in manufacturing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
services are not necessarily less innovative than manufacturing.

innovation in services is not only real, but is also a source of economic growth and employment, as well as a key to the development of new forms of organisation, new modes of production, new types of work, and new social relationships.
the innovation process in services is not fundamentally different from that in manufacturing, although there are differences in emphasis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the service sector is a dynamic and heterogeneous sector, which has a high capacity for innovation.
innovation in services is a reality, but that the forms it takes and the way it is organised are still poorly understood.
the differences in the nature and characteristics of goods and services are more important than their similarities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the service economy is not a homogeneous entity.
the innovation process in services is characterised by a number of specific features that need to be taken into account when designing policies to support innovation.
innovation in services is not a new phenomenon, although the way in which it is organised has changed.
